(2)

questions.stem:
The function f is defined by
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = \frac{x+3}{x-4} \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}, x \neq 4$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find $\mathrm{ff}(6)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $x=6$ into f and substitutes the result back into f to find a value for $\mathrm{ff}(6)$. Alternatively substitutes $x=6$ into $\mathrm{ff}(x)=\dfrac{\left(\frac{x+3}{x-4}\right)+3}{\left(\frac{x+3}{x-4}\right)-4}$ condoning slips.
A1: 15

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Changes the subject of $y=\dfrac{x+3}{x-4}$ or $x=\dfrac{y+3}{y-4}$ to $y=\dfrac{\dots x\pm3}{\dots x\pm1}$ or $x=\dfrac{\dots y\pm3}{\dots y\pm1}$
A1: Achieves $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{4x+3}{x-1}$. Accept $\mathrm{f}^{-1}=\dots$ or $y=\dots$ instead of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\dots$
B1: $x \neq 1$. The omission of $x \in \mathbb{R}$ is condoned. Accept alternative notations.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The function g is defined by
$$\mathrm{g}(x)=x^2+5 \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}, x>0$$
(c) Find the exact value of $a$ for which
$$\mathrm{gf}(a)=7$$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Correct attempt to set up an equation in x or a. This will usually be $\left(\frac{x+3}{x-4}\right)^2+5=7$ but $\mathrm{f}(a)=\mathrm{g}^{-1}(7)$ may be used first. Score when a suitable equation is set up and allow if a minor slip or miscopy is made if the intention is clear.

Alternatively, uses $(\mathrm{f}(x))^2+5=7 \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(x)=(\pm)\sqrt{2}$ and their part (b) leading to $a=\mathrm{f}^{-1}(\sqrt{2})=\frac{4\sqrt{2}+3}{\sqrt{2}-1}$. questions.stem:
A new mobile phone is released for sale.
The total sales $N$ of this phone, in **thousands**, is modelled by the equation
$$N=125-A\mathrm{e}^{-0.109t} \qquad t \geqslant 0$$
where $A$ is a constant and $t$ is the time in months after the phone was released for sale.
Given that when $t=0$, $N=32$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) state the value of $A$.
(1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that when $t=T$ the total sales of the phone was $100\,000$
(b) find, according to the model, the value of $T$. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Sets $100=125-"93"\mathrm{e}^{-0.109T}$ and proceeds to $A\mathrm{e}^{-0.109T}=\dots$. May use t instead of T. Condone slips.
dM1: Uses correct order of operations and correct log work from an equation of the form $A\mathrm{e}^{kT}=B$, $AB>0$ to proceed to a value for T (must be a solvable equation). Implied by a correct answer for their equation.
A1: 12.05 cao
Note: Candidates who use 100000 in the equation will score no marks in this part.
Note: Answer only with no working sent to review, but 12.05 following a correct equation seen score M1dM1A1.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find, according to the model, the rate of increase in total sales when $t=7$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.)
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:

Award for an expression of the form $\dots\mathrm{e}^{-0.109\times7}$ if no incorrect working is seen. The substitution of $t=7$ may be implied by a correct value for their derivative of correct form.

Note: Answer only scores no marks.

$$y=\frac{\ln(x^2+k)}{x^2+k} \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}$$
where $k$ is a positive constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{Ax\left(B-\ln(x^2+k)\right)}{(x^2+k)^2}$$
where $A$ and $B$ are constants to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to apply the quotient rule. Score for an expression of the form $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{(x^2+k)\times\frac{\dots}{x^2+k}-Qx\ln(x^2+k)}{(x^2+k)^2}$ oe (may be simplified) where $\dots$ is P or Px and P,Q>0. May also attempt the product rule, in which case look for $-Px(x^2+k)^{-2}\ln(x^2+k)+(x^2+k)^{-1}\times\frac{\dots}{x^2+k}$ where $\dots$ is Q or Qx and P,Q>0

questions.stem:
An area of sea floor is being monitored.
The area of the sea floor, $S\,\mathrm{km}^2$, covered by coral reefs is modelled by the equation
$$S=pq^t$$
where $p$ and $q$ are constants and $t$ is the number of years after monitoring began.
Given that
$$\log_{10}S=4.5-0.006t$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find, according to the model, the area of sea floor covered by coral reefs when $t=2$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes in $t=2$ and proceeds to find a value for S via $10^{\dots}$. May be implied by a correct value for their equation. Note awrt 24000 may arise from a slip with $0.006\times2=0.12$, and is acceptable for M1.
A1: awrt $30800\,\mathrm{km}^2$ including units, from correct work and isw as long as units are included with a correct value. But e.g. 30760 followed by 307 km$^2$ is A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find a complete equation for the model in the form
$$S=pq^t$$
giving the value of $p$ and the value of $q$ each to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Writes $S=10^{4.5-0.006t}$ or award for either $(p=)10^{4.5}$ or $(q=)10^{-0.006}$ even if from an incorrect step. Essentially for knowing they need to raise to base 10. May arise from attempts at solving simultaneous equations using the answer to (a) (allowing for rounding errors).
dM1: Writes $S=10^{4.5}\times(10^{-0.006})^t$ or award for both $p=10^{4.5}$ and $q=10^{-0.006}$ (oe forms e.g. accept $\left(\frac{1}{10^{0.006}}\right)$ or $\left(\frac{1}{1.01}\right)$ for q) Must be fully correct method to this point but allow if all that is wrong is rounding errors from other methods such solving simultaneous equations (e.g. $0.990^t$).
A1cso: $S=31600\times(0.986)^t$ Must be awrt 3 s.f. values. Must be an equation including the S, not just p and q values, but accept if seen in (c).

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) With reference to the model, interpret the value of the constant $q$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: E.g. accept the following or variations of them: The proportion of area covered by coral reefs retained from year to year. The seafloor covered by coral reduces by 1.4% each year. The proportional change/decrease in sea floor area covered by coral reefs per year. Do not accept "rate of change" or "decrease in area of reefs per year" or "q is the gradient" as the answer as it is an incorrect interpretation. There must be reference to, or equivalents of, the following: sea floor area or sea floor or area or seabed; coral reefs or coral or reef; each year or year to year or per year; (q or its value is) a percentage/proportional decrease/remaining.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- The proportional change should be conveyed.
- Some acceptable answers: After 1 year the area will reduce to S last year times q. It shows the speed that coral reefs seafloor reduce. The percentage of remaining area of sea floor covered by coral reefs to the area of that covered last year. q represents the proportion of decreasing of the area of sea floor covered by coral reefs every year.
- Some unacceptable answers: When there is extra t, the S will increase one more unit of 0.986. q means the percentage of the part of sea floor covered by coral reefs after t years. q is the amount of coral reefs die/shrink in accordance to time. The area of the sea floor is decreasing at almost 0.986 times before. For every increase in the value of t, the total area of coral reefs will decrease in a rate of $0.986^t$

parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to substitute in $x=\frac{1}{4}$ and rearranges to find an exact value for y. Look for $y=M\arcsin\left(\pm\frac{1}{2}\right)\to k\pi$ or $k(30°)$ allowing errors in dividing by the 4, or equivalents criteria via a double angle identity, correct up to sign error.
A1: $\frac{\pi}{24}$. Ignore extra solutions outside the domain.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to differentiate achieving a form $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}=\right)A\sin4y\cos4y$ or $A\sin8y$ oe. Accept alternative forms e.g. via implicit differentiation $1=A\sin4y\cos4y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$. The $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}$ may be missing, or labelled $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ for this mark.
A1: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}=8\sin4y\cos4y$ oe eg $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}=4\sin8y$ Coefficients must be simplified. Must include the $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (b) Alt: $x=\sin^24y\Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{4}\arcsin\sqrt{x}\Rightarrow\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\sqrt{x})^2}}\times\frac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ M1; $\frac{dx}{dy}=8\sqrt{x}\sqrt{1-x}$ A1. Alt by finding y first. Mark (b) and (c) together via such approaches. But note that part (c) says "Hence" and the reciprocal law must have been used at some stage to score full marks. M1: Makes y the subject and differentiates to reach form $\frac{dy}{dx}=A\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\sqrt{x})^2}}\times\dots$ where … is a function of x. A1: For $\frac{dx}{dy}=8\sqrt{x}\sqrt{1-x}$ oe with square roots combined. Coefficients must have been gathered.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence show that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ can be written in the form
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{q+r(x+s)^2}}$$
where $q$, $r$ and $s$ are constants to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Uses $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=1\div\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}$ (allow for the reciprocal of their answer to (b) if left hand side is omitted). Variables must be consistent.
M1: Attempts to use $\sin4y=\pm\sqrt{x}$ and $\cos4y=\pm\sqrt{1-x}$ to write $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ or $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}$ in terms of x only with no trig terms.
A1: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{16-64\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}}$ and isw after correct answer. Allow with terms under the square root reversed.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (c) Alt: M1: For use of the reciprocal rule of derivatives evidenced in the working – allow for it being used in (b) to find $\frac{dx}{dy}$ from $\frac{dy}{dx}$. M1: Award for the correct procedure of having made y the subject and differentiating to reach the correct form for the answer, ie $\frac{dy}{dx}=A\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\sqrt{x})^2}}\times Bx^{-\frac{1}{2}}$. A1: As main scheme.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Using the answer to part (c),
(d) (i) state the $x$ coordinate of the point where the value of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ is a minimum,
(ii) state the value of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at this point.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) B1ft: $\left(x=\right)\frac{1}{2}$ ft their $-s$ provided their $q>0$, their $r<0$ and their x is in the range $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1$.
(ii) B1ft: $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\right)\frac{1}{4}$ ft their q provided it is positive and their r was negative.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (d) Note to score marks in (d) they must have a derivative which does have a minimum and is of a completed square form (the r may be inside the bracket) or in some other way clearly uses their (c) (e.g. minimising their quadratic).

The point $P$ with $x$ coordinate $\frac{1}{4}$ lies on $C$
(a) Find the exact $y$ coordinate of $P$

where $q$, $r$ and $s$ are constants to be found.
(3)

(ii) state the value of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at this point.
(2)
